item.title: Illustrated Library Checkout Cards
item.description: In the olden days, library checkouts were completed without computer intervention with the use of cards that were signed by patrons and stamped with due dates by library staff. For over a decade, artist Heidi Pitre, who is based in Kansas City, has taken these old cards and used them for art projects. item.title: Watch Humanoid Robots Dancing with Children in an Elaborate Production Number
item.description: The annual Spring Festival Gala is a "must see" TV experience in China, broadcast on the eve of the Lunar New year. This year's show featured dancing by humanoid robots developed by several Chinese robotics firms. The robots danced, flipped, jumped, and performed martial arts moves. Only one fell, and that turned out to be a programmed stunt. item.title: A Magnificent Ruin in an Obscure City
item.description: The city of Hampi is in the Indian state of Karnataka, and its ruins are a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Five hundred years ago, Hampi was the biggest city in India, and the second largest city in the world, but today relatively few people outside of India are familiar with it. One of its stone ruins is pictured above- what kind of building was this? It's magnificently ornate, and huge. Check the size of the people standing in front. item.title: A New Star in Olympic Cross-country Skiing has Emerged
item.description: The eyes of the world were drawn to an Olympic preliminary qualifying round in the women's cross-country skiing event in Tésero, Italy, on Wednesday. A large dog joined in the race and was even caught on Omega's official timekeeping camera as he crossed the finish line. Local news outlets and social media lit up at the appearance of what looked like a wolf running the race. But this wolf was wearing a collar. item.description: This unassuming building in Millmont, Pennsylvania, looks like nothing more than a garage specializing in oil changes. item.title: This Purse Looks Like a Dumpling
item.description: Design Boom introduces to us this delicious handbag made by Esenes Worldwide, a fashion house in New York City. Control your hunger because it's not edible unless you're really committed. The company is selling 150 of these unusual purses priced at $150 each.The leather has been carefully shaped while hot to give it the same wringled and irregular texture of a dumpling. item.title: "Smart Underwear" Can Measure Human Farts
item.description: Embed from Getty ImagesHow often do you fart? Is that more or less than the average healthy human? Who knows? Scientists aren't quite sure, yet, but that could change with new technology. Brantley Hall of the University of Maryland led a team in developing a special device to answer the question. It attaches to your underwear and then detects certain gases that indicate flatulence. They named the device "Smart Underwear," even though you have to provide your own underwear. item.title: Tony the Frog is an Escape Artist
item.description: Most people become disgusted when they find a foreign object in their food, and even more so when that object is alive. Musician Simon Curtis, on the other hand, didn't lose it when he found a frog in his lettuce. Making a simple salad in the middle of the night turned out to be an adventure he never expected.
